A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–B support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original multilingual intervention experiments, compliance rates, representation analyses and jailbreak-vector experiments, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds refusal-vector addition experiments, layer/token diagnostics and capability-preservation comparisons.

M1.justification: Difference-in-means extraction, refusal-score ranking, KL filtering and activation interventions remain substantively unchanged. The addition experiments in Section 5.4 test the procedure already described in v1, Equation 5.

E1.justification: Table 8 adds MMLU, WikiText language modeling and ARC-C evaluation, substantially extending task coverage to general knowledge, language modeling and reasoning capabilities. The original 14-language PolyRefuse coverage is retained.

E2.justification: New Table 8 compares the selected refusal vector against two alternative candidate difference-in-means vectors, labeled Random vector 1 and 2, alongside the unmodified model. Existing comparisons retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: v2 adds inverse-intervention evaluation using English, German and Thai refusal vectors and a four-condition Llama-3.1-8B capability comparison with additional metrics. Existing sampling sizes, WildGuard evaluation, model configurations and the 0.2 KL threshold remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 adds direct tests of whether refusal-vector addition suppresses compliance. Appendix A.5 substantially expands diagnostic evidence through layer/token sensitivity plots and controls testing whether selected-vector ablation preserves capabilities better than alternative-vector ablation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The added curves describe layer/token variation, without introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds compliance-reduction results, selection-diagnostic curves and capability results while retaining the original numerical tables and plotted outcomes. In the new Table 8 comparison, selected-vector ablation changes refusal rate from 0.99 to 0.02, MMLU from 68.5 to 68.0, perplexity from 8.65 to 8.71 and ARC-C from 52.4 to 52.5. These are newly reported within-v2 comparisons.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and intervention formulations retain their substance. Equation 4 removes the refusal vector's layer subscript, matching the existing single-selected-vector description. No new theorem, proof or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims of refusal-direction universality across safety-aligned languages and geometric explanations of multilingual vulnerabilities. New experiments provide additional support without redefining the central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 6 qualifies the analysis as concerning the refusal-extraction layer and distinguishes downstream refusal from harmfulness identification. It also explains Yoruba's silhouette scores using cluster compactness and clarifies that PCA arrows are illustrative rather than strictly centroid-derived. The existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: Figures 10–15 disclose additional model/language-specific extraction-layer and token choices, including token identities for Qwen. Table 8 specifies the alternative controls' layer/token locations. These expand documentation of the existing selection procedure; the code-access information is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds representation-engineering citations to Xu et al. and Li et al., cites Zhao et al. on separate harmfulness/refusal representations, and adds references for the capability benchmarks. The overall positioning around multilingual refusal mechanisms remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 adds Sections 5.4 and A.5, expands explanations in Section 6, reverses the English/German example order in Appendix B, and updates affiliation and conference information. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the multilingual addition chart in Figure 3, a substantial suite of layer/token diagnostic plots in Figures 10–15, and capability Table 8. Existing displays are largely retained and repositioned; Figure 2's palette changes, and Table 5 moves closer to its related analysis.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens validation through inverse interventions and direct capability-preservation controls, addressing gaps in v1's empirical support. Its qualifications about harmfulness, refusal and illustrative arrows also improve interpretation. The gains are bounded: capability testing covers one model, and detailed settings and uncertainty reporting remain limited.
